title: SLO Arbitration Engine and Error-Budget Transfer Playbook for Multi-Region Model Endpoints
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We operate model endpoints with multiple regional replicas, several model variants (quantized/float32), and heterogeneous tenant priorities. Current SLO declarations are static per-route and conflict during regional capacity constraints: some routes consume error budget aggressively while others silently fail. Goal: define an arbitration engine and a documented playbook that (1) declares canonical SLIs per endpoint+model variant, (2) defines a deterministic algorithm to reconcile competing SLOs across regions and tenants, and (3) implements an auditable error-budget transfer and staged load-shedding policy together with circuit-breaker thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI set created for all public endpoints and top-10 model variants (latency, availability, and quality metrics).
Arbitration algorithm documented and reviewed: inputs include tenant priority, model quality delta, regional capacity factor, and remaining error budget. Formula and pseudo-code included.
Error-budget transfer policy implemented as a JSON-declarative rule set and can be applied by the traffic-orchestrator. Transfers are time-bounded and audit-logged.
Circuit-breaker thresholds and staged load-shedding bands implemented for each route with clear fallbacks to compatible model variants.
Dashboards and alerting added: burn-rate, transfer events, per-tenant degradation, and post-failover quality regressions.
Runbook updated with example incidents and operator steps; chaos test demonstrating graceful degradation executed in staging.
decisions: Adopt a weighted-arbitration formula: score = w_tenant * priority + w_quality * quality_delta - w_capacity * (1 - region_capacity). Default weights: w_tenant=0.5, w_quality=0.3, w_capacity=0.2.

Error-budget transfers are allowed only when donor endpoint has >30% remaining error budget for 24h and receiver is in critical state (burn-rate > 4x). Transfers capped to 15% of donor's budget per 6h. All transfers must be recorded and reversible.
Circuit-breaker stages: WARN (soft throttling), SHED (load-shedding low-priority requests), FALLBACK (route to lower-cost variant), EJECT (regional ejection and traffic reroute).
Quality SLI will be measured using a rolling promptset pass-rate (A/B evaluation harness) and hashed per-tenant promptset for privacy. Threshold: quality SLI >= 92% for primary model variants.
telemetry_queries: SQL (events): SELECT route, model_variant, AVG(eval_pass) as quality FROM model_evals WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1h' GROUP BY route, model_variant
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish playbook and canonical SLI definitions; collect comments from SRE, Product, and Trust teams.
Week 1: Implement arbitration engine in staging behind a feature flag; simulate transfers using recorded traffic.
Week 2: Run controlled chaos (region ejection, model spike) and validate transfer caps, audit logs, and fallback correctness.
Week 3: Gradual rollout to 10% of production traffic; monitor burn-rate and quality regressions.
Rollback criteria: unexpected quality drop >2% for any tenant or transfer events not reversible within 30m.
test_plan: Unit tests for arbitration score and transfer caps with edge cases (zero capacity, negative quality delta).
Integration test: end-to-end with traffic-orchestrator applying a transfer and verifying audit log entry.
Staging chaos scenario: simulate regional capacity drop to 30% and ensure correct staged shedding and model fallback.
Load test: synthetic 10k rps per region while ensuring SLO score ordering is stable under jitter.

risks: Incorrect weight tuning could bias transfers to low-quality variants, causing silent quality regressions.
Audit log volume could be high during large-scale transfers; ensure retention and storage limits considered.
Transfers introduce coupling between endpoints; cascading transfers could amplify failures if donor budgets are misestimated.
followups: Post-launch: run a 30-day analysis of transferred budgets and customer quality impact, produce a tuning report.
Quarterly: revisit default weights and transfer caps; add ML-optimized weight tuning if manual weights show drift.
Add a governance UI in Console for viewing pending/active transfers and manual overrides for enterprise customers.
